Risk-based proportionality, actual internal and external staffing needs and adaptation to changed circumstances, not size-only exemption.
Nondelegable collective responsibility for sound effective governance, risk management and internal control despite portfolio allocation.

Documented continuously appropriate materiality thresholds at least underwriting/market/credit/liquidity/operational; consider sustainability/concentration and others where relevant, not accounting/legal-breach impacts alone; uniform application.
Shared risk understanding and language, responsibility/incentives/open dialogue, board example and communication, evaluation and remediation.

Group-wide controls/information/culture; foreign/noninsurance risks and corporate-law influence, cooperation, consistent implementation and involvement of smaller entities while retaining entity duties.

Clear duties/substitutes/reporting and separation of risk taking from control, proportionate conflict safeguards; risk-based process/control/escalation mapping and staff knowledge; current documentation and prior versions retained; group adaptation and entity responsibility.

Timely regular/ad-hoc upward and decision feedback, active supervisory board and group interaction; at least two actual managers before material decisions, insurer-defined materiality, reconstructible proportionate decision records, forward-looking governance review and documented follow-up.

Accessible coherent written/digital policies with interfaces, information/function rights and implemented processes; separate adoption by entities, board first/material approval, annual statutory-policy review and ad-hoc triggers; documented outcomes, staff communication and compliance controls.

Identify and document risk-bearing automated underwriting/claims/administration, accountable intervention and board understanding; pre-use and ongoing quality assurance, regular proportionate independent evaluation. Conditional scope/nonapplicability externally qualified.

Four key functions plus qualified additional key tasks; equal standing, resources/access/direct reporting; each function has exactly one internally responsible natural person, qualified combinations and conflicts; annual and severe-event reports and reciprocal timely information, including group/entity functions.

Risk-based laws/regulation/material recognised external-standard monitoring; known internal controls, officer responsibilities do not erase compliance oversight; advice/legal-change monitoring, risk identification and current plan, annual and severe-event reporting.

Separate statutory actuary and actuarial-function roles, conflict-controlled calculation/validation, methods/data/obligations/change effects, future profit-sharing and national/group consultation; data defects/remedies and external data, underwriting/reinsurance transfer stress and long-term guarantee premium adequacy; understandable annual function report, no blanket unchanged statement or partial-report substitution.

Audit required in every undertaking covering whole governance/outsourcing; assurance priority over advice, direct unedited reporting and independence from operations and improper influence; historical conditional key-function combination does not revive deleted2027 DR271(2).

URCF implements and monitors risk system/profile/limits, assesses strategy/methods and promotes awareness, coordinates ORSA, advises remediation; annual/ad-hoc reporting may use suitable complete ORSA content but must separately cover omitted material system issues.

Board-owned annual risk strategy/appetite and operative limits; coherent policies and insurer-specific stress scenarios/triggers/assumptions/actions; IT/legal-change/sustainability operational risks, internal/external loss events, new-product analysis, credit/basis/transfer/liquidity/termination risk in mitigation and meaningful risk-sensitive quantitative analysis. Insurer develops stress models.

Group board risk strategy/appetite/tolerance, consistent but entity-adopted implementation, all group/transaction/concentration/reputation/interdependency risks including third-country and unregulated entities.

Risk-proportionate embedded controls including outsourcing, documented frequency/scope/results and required information; continuous suitability monitoring, annual board report plus material-defect ad-hoc reporting and timely adjustment.

Qualify outsourcing versus occasional services using substance/duration/frequency without invented cutoffs; retain nondelegable board duties and separation, third-country access/privacy; pre-contract and ongoing risk analysis including concentration/subdelegation/provider/exit/continuity/legal risks and material-change decisions.

Critical/important and partial-function qualification; key functions/tasks always important, typical core areas assessed; board pre-approval/subdelegation approval, prompt sufficiently concrete intent notice with draft, pre2016 contract inventory and timely adaptation.

Key-function/task outsourcing officer independently oversees provider with preserved board information; no report bypass, qualified combinations/time/conflicts, no identity with responsible provider person. Officer is not the outsourced audit function itself.

No automatic lower diligence/noncritical classification; qualified service-level agreements and proportionate provider assessment, conflicts always checked, avoid automatic provider choice, map each legal entity/provider/function.

Ordinary intermediary without authority differs from delegated underwriting/claims; important outsourcing and partial/aggregate scope, broker-claims legal restriction. Lifecycle policies cover provider finance/technology/capacity/control/conflicts, continuity/exit and important-function contingency transfer/reintegration.

Board-approved risk-specific contingency plans including outsourcing and tolerable downtime/recovery; tested effectiveness, embedded clear responsibilities/escalation/information, known and emergency-accessible plans.
